I spent the past hour researching some alternatives to back up files and decided to share my research results. I'm not a particularly tech inclined person, so feel free to correct me if I make mistakes.

Cloud
Great if you have a home server or trust some business to protect your files. I don't, so this option was out.

Portable external hard drives
These HDDs (hard disc drives) save your data on spinning disks. Moving parts fail, especially if there is any chance you might drop them. Reviews suggest that regardless of your brand/model choice, you should expect yours to fail within 3 years, maybe as soon as 2 months. If you are looking at long-term storage (such as photos you want for the rest of your life), these are out.

DIY portable external hard drives
Place a typically internal SSD in a case. SSD = solid state drive. No moving parts, so less prone to failure. They do wear out when being rewritten. Drives might last for 1,000-10,000 rewrites. This is a good option if you have large files or would like to simultaneously access a large quantity of files (>256 GB). These also have faster write times than traditional external HDD drives or USB sticks (see below). If you want to store your photos/music/movies and regularly view/stream them, this is your best option. It's affordable ($100-$200 or less for 1TB or more), and it's very easy - buy a case ($10 or less) and buy a hard drive. Put hard drive in case. Viola, you made your own external hard drive.

USB flash drives
USB drives also use SSDs, so they are good for long-term storage. They read/write more slowly than a DIY external, but are affordable for small files (documents, small spreadsheets, etc) or rarely accessed files (You know, photos from that vacation with your ex in 2009). At the moment, you can get USB flash drives that can store 32GB for $10, 128GB for $25 and 256GB for $50. (Source: newegg.com)

Optical discs (CDs, DVDs) To be thorough, optical discs can also be used for long-term storage as they won't fail due to age alone, although they store less than USB flash drives and are not always compatible with new laptops.
